title: Drumming as timekeeping and his cymbal style
summary: He thinks of drums as timekeeping, favors snare, and describes his own light cymbal and Chinese block ideas.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: In the orchestra, is there anything else you can tell about the way you think of your drums? Is it mainly as a timekeeper to fill in, or what do you think of your...

Well, I think a drum, yeah. That's a part to you. I figured a drum is mostly a timekeeping instrument. It's strictly a time instrument, you know what I mean? And you just feel your own ideas, how they, you know, different numbers. You play, you understand the feeling. I think in the line of playing jazz music, you've managed to use plenty of snare drums. In less cymbal way. Yeah, it's a day all these young kids always playing cymbals. Yeah, a snare drum feels a band move. In a line of small bands, it really feels move, a snare drum. And years ago, we played mostly snare drums. And make your bells and your chonny in between breaks, and use your cry cymbals going out. Open them or you choke them. Going out, you see. And when they come out, first with the overhead socks, then first they had the flow sock cymbals. That didn't last a lot. We used to call them flow beaters. But that didn't last, and they went over to, people called them the hi-hat cymbals. We called them sock cymbals. Sometimes a man might play that choke that, you know, on his drums. You know, to play it nice and soft. A person's singing or something like that. Some guys might use a stick and one wire brush. Different ideas. It's just different ideas of different drummers, yeah. Now I adopt the idea of playing with my cymbal, choke, and this play light on the two sticks, and the public took to that. They like it. Yeah, I started that idea. I started that idea, my own idea. And people took to that. Some liked to hear me play on the Chinese block with one stick and just play on the cymbal. Because they tell me they do that. At the old Absinthe House. They like that, you know. And just play Chinese block with like a little light rhythm on there, you know. And just take one hand, the left hand, and just beat on the cymbal, tap that light, and they get kicks out of that. That was my idea. They just took to that. Some wanted to play some number all the way through on the bell. There's one car bell. Yeah.
